title: 投資是藝術，目標是勝過市場
en: Investing Is an Art; the Goal Is to Beat the Market

vocab.example: One of the most important things to bear in mind today is that economics isn’t an exact science.
vocab.def: 提醒對方別忘了某件重要的事，比 remember 更帶有「請牢記」的意味。
vocab.exzh: 今天最需要記住的重要事情之一，就是經濟學並不是一門精確的科學。

vocab.example: past results can be replicated with confidence
vocab.def: 在科學裡，指另一個人照同樣條件做實驗，能得到同樣結果。課文說經濟學做不到。
vocab.exzh: 過去的結果可以放心地重現

vocab.meaning: 使例行化、變成固定流程
vocab.example: it’s never my goal—in this book or elsewhere—to suggest it can be routinized.
vocab.def: 把需要判斷的事變成機械式的固定流程。作者強調投資不應該這樣。
vocab.exzh: 不論在這本書或其他地方，我的目標都絕不是暗示投資可以變成例行公事。

vocab.meaning: 憑直覺的、靠直覺判斷的
vocab.example: how essential it is that one’s investment approach be intuitive and adaptive rather than be fixed and mechanistic.
vocab.def: intuition 是直覺。作者說投資方法必須有直覺成分，而不是照表操課。
vocab.exzh: 一個人的投資方法必須憑直覺且能隨機應變，而不是固定且機械化，這一點有多麼重要。

vocab.meaning: 能適應的、能隨機應變的
vocab.example: how essential it is that one’s investment approach be intuitive and adaptive rather than be fixed and mechanistic.
vocab.def: adapt（適應）的形容詞。環境會變，所以方法也要跟著調整。
vocab.exzh: 一個人的投資方法必須憑直覺且能隨機應變，而不是固定且機械化，這一點有多麼重要。

vocab.example: how essential it is that one’s investment approach be intuitive and adaptive rather than be fixed and mechanistic.
vocab.def: 像機器一樣照固定規則運作，沒有彈性。與 intuitive、adaptive 相對。
vocab.exzh: 一個人的投資方法必須憑直覺且能隨機應變，而不是固定且機械化，這一點有多麼重要。

vocab.example: At bottom, it’s a matter of what you’re trying to accomplish.
vocab.def: 指到最核心、最根本的地方，相當於 fundamentally。常放在句首，引出最根本的看法。
vocab.exzh: 說到底，這取決於你想達成什麼。

vocab.example: just invest in an index fund that buys a little of everything.
vocab.def: 追蹤某個市場指數的基金，買進指數內大致所有的股票，因此只能拿到市場平均的報酬。
vocab.exzh: 只要投資一檔指數型基金，它每樣都買一點。

vocab.example: That will give you what is known as “market returns”—merely matching whatever the market does.
vocab.def: 整個市場平均的報酬率。作者的定義：只是和市場表現打平，沒有超越。
vocab.exzh: 那會給你所謂的「市場報酬」——只是和市場的表現打平。

vocab.example: Counting on luck isn’t much of a plan, so you’d better concentrate on insight.
vocab.def: 把希望放在某人或某事上。count on luck 是「指望運氣」，作者認為這不算計畫。
vocab.exzh: 指望運氣算不上什麼像樣的計畫，所以你最好專心培養洞察力。

vocab.example: To accomplish that, you need either good luck or superior insight.
vocab.def: 看穿事物本質、別人沒看到的見解。作者認為這才是勝過市場的來源，但很難教。
vocab.exzh: 要做到這一點，你需要好運，或是卓越的洞察力。

vocab.example: that necessary “trace of wisdom” that Ben Graham so eloquently calls for.
vocab.def: 說得清楚又有說服力。so eloquently 帶有欽佩的語氣，是在稱讚 Graham 的措辭。
vocab.exzh: 就是班傑明・葛拉漢措辭如此精采地要求的那一絲必要的智慧。

sentences.en: One of the most important things to bear in mind today is that economics isn’t an exact science.
sentences.zh: 今天最需要記住的重要事情之一，就是經濟學並不是一門精確的科學。

meta.src: 出自備忘錄 “WILL IT WORK?” MARCH 5, 2009

sentences.en: It may not even be much of a science at all, in the sense that in science, controlled experiments can be conducted, past results can be replicated with confidence, and cause-and-effect relationships can be depended on to hold.
sentences.zh: 它甚至可能算不上什麼科學，因為在科學裡，可以進行受控實驗，過去的結果可以放心地重現，因果關係也可以信賴它會成立。

meta.src: 出自備忘錄 “WILL IT WORK?” MARCH 5, 2009

sentences.en: Because investing is at least as much art as it is science, it’s never my goal—in this book or elsewhere—to suggest it can be routinized.
sentences.zh: 因為投資至少有一半是藝術、一半是科學，所以不論在這本書或其他地方，我的目標都絕不是暗示投資可以變成例行公事。

sentences.en: In fact, one of the things I most want to emphasize is how essential it is that one’s investment approach be intuitive and adaptive rather than be fixed and mechanistic.
sentences.zh: 事實上，我最想強調的事情之一，就是一個人的投資方法必須憑直覺且能隨機應變，而不是固定且機械化，這一點有多麼重要。

sentences.en: At bottom, it’s a matter of what you’re trying to accomplish.
sentences.zh: 說到底，這取決於你想達成什麼。

sentences.en: Anyone can achieve average investment performance—just invest in an index fund that buys a little of everything.
sentences.zh: 任何人都能取得平均的投資表現——只要投資一檔指數型基金，它每樣都買一點。

sentences.en: That will give you what is known as “market returns”—merely matching whatever the market does.
sentences.zh: 那會給你所謂的「市場報酬」——只是和市場的表現打平。
但成功的投資人想要更多。

sentences.en: They want to beat the market.
In my view, that’s the definition of successful investing: doing better than the market and other investors.
sentences.zh: 依我之見，這就是成功投資的定義：做得比市場和其他投資人更好。

sentences.en: To accomplish that, you need either good luck or superior insight.
sentences.zh: 要做到這一點，你需要好運，或是卓越的洞察力。

sentences.en: Counting on luck isn’t much of a plan, so you’d better concentrate on insight.
sentences.zh: 指望運氣算不上什麼像樣的計畫，所以你最好專心培養洞察力。

sentences.en: In basketball they say, “You can’t coach height,” meaning all the coaching in the world won’t make a player taller.
sentences.zh: 在籃球界有句話：「身高是教不來的」，意思是不管再多的訓練，都不能讓球員變得更高。

sentences.en: It’s almost as hard to teach insight.
sentences.zh: 要教會別人洞察力，幾乎一樣困難。

sentences.en: As with any other art form, some people just understand investing better than others.
sentences.zh: 就像任何其他藝術一樣，有些人就是比別人更懂投資。

sentences.en: They have—or manage to acquire—that necessary “trace of wisdom” that Ben Graham so eloquently calls for.
sentences.zh: 他們擁有——或是設法取得——班傑明・葛拉漢措辭如此精采地要求的那一絲必要的智慧。

grammar.point: 要求、重要性之後的 that 子句：用原形動詞
grammar.quote: In fact, one of the things I most want to emphasize is how essential it is that one’s investment approach be intuitive and adaptive rather than be fixed and mechanistic.
grammar.explain:
how essential it is that … 後面的 that 子句用 be，而不是 is。這是「假設語氣的原形動詞」：在 essential、important、vital、necessary 這類形容詞之後的 that 子句，動詞一律用原形（即使主詞是第三人稱單數）。
另外，rather than be fixed 是 rather than ＋ 原形動詞，與前面的 be intuitive 並列。

grammar.point: not much of a ＋ 名詞：算不上什麼像樣的…
grammar.quote: Counting on luck isn’t much of a plan, so you’d better concentrate on insight.
grammar.explain:
not much of a plan 的意思是「算不上什麼好計畫」，是委婉的批評。同樣用法：He’s not much of a singer（他唱得不怎麼樣）。
前面第 1 段的 It may not even be much of a science 也是同一個結構。
另外 you’d better ＋ 原形是 you had better，語氣是「你最好…（否則會有麻煩）」，比 should 強。

grammar.quote: As with any other art form, some people just understand investing better than others.
grammar.explain:
As with X, S ＋ V 是常用的開頭，意思是「就像 X 一樣，…」，用來把一件事類比到另一件事。
better than others 的 others 是 other people，比較對象被省略成單純的「別人」。
